children: Mumbai: General Insurance Corporation of India (GIC Re), the country's largest reinsurer, reported a 14.35% year-on-year decline in net profit to 2,455 crore for the quarter ended September 2026 due to deterioration in the underwriting performance.

During the same period in the previous year, the reinsurer had reported net profit of 2,866 crore. Gross written premium increased 16.96% to 11,228 crore from 9,600 crore a year earlier. The reinsurer's underwriting loss widened to 985 crore in the September quarter from 387 crore in the year-ago period, while its combined ratio deteriorated sharply to 110.23% from 109.15%, indicating higher claims and expenses against premiums earned. The deterioration in underwriting performance was in its domestic business, where the incurred claims ratio rose to 107% from 104% in the corresponding period last year.

title: GIC Re Q2 Net Profit Slips 14%
